hook.from: Geography > Location, Terrain, Natural resources; Economy > Exports
hook.excerpt: Southern Africa, island in the Indian Ocean, about 800 km (500 mi) east of Madagascar || small coastal plain rising to discontinuous mountains encircling central plateau || the main island, from which the country derives its name, is of volcanic origin and is almost entirely surrounded by coral reefs; former home of the extinct dodo, a large flightless bird related to pigeons || Resources: arable land, fish || Exports: fish, garments, raw sugar, fertilizers, diamonds (2023)

physicalGeography.excerpt: small coastal plain rising to discontinuous mountains encircling central plateau || Southern Africa, island in the Indian Ocean, about 800 km (500 mi) east of Madagascar

climate.excerpt: tropical, modified by southeast trade winds; warm, dry winter (May to November); hot, wet, humid summer (November to May) || cyclones (November to April); almost completely surrounded by reefs that may pose maritime hazards

economy.excerpt: upper middle-income Indian Ocean island economy; diversified portfolio; investing in maritime security; strong tourism sector decimated by COVID-19; expanding in information and financial services; environmentally fragile || Exports: fish, garments, raw sugar, fertilizers, diamonds (2023) || Industries: food processing (largely sugar milling), textiles, clothing, mining, chemicals, metal products, transport equipment, nonelectrical machinery, tourism

peopleAndCulture.excerpt: Creole 86.5%, Bhojpuri 5.3%, French 4.1%, two languages 1.4%, other 2.6% (includes English, one of the two official languages of the National Assembly, which is spoken by less than 1% of the population), unspecified 0.1% (2011 est.) || Hindu 48.5%, Roman Catholic 26.3%, Muslim 17.3%, other Christian 6.4%, other 0.6%, none 0.7%, unspecified 0.1% (2011 est.) || Indo-Mauritian (compose approximately two thirds of the total population), Creole, Sino-Mauritian, Franco-Mauritian
